source.title: Geometric Alignment without Functional Equivalence: A Layer-wise Analysis of the Speech-Text Modality Gap
source.authors: Ming-Hao Hsu; Xiaohai Tian; Jun Zhang; Lu Lu; Yuxuan Wang; Zhizheng Wu

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures paired speech–text representation geometry and answer formation, and its results specifically qualify the inference that geometric alignment implies functional equivalence. It does not test whether alignment increases with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The study’s own CKA measurements, paired answer-margin results, and DTW-setting sensitivity bear on cross-modal alignment and its interpretation. Benchmark accuracy comparisons, compression repairs, attention edits, and probe results are not separately recorded as convergence rows: they do not directly measure whether representations converge across scale or systems. Results cited from prior work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures speech–text alignment inside each speech LLM: the speech and text routes of one model, sharing one LLM backbone. It does not compare independently trained models, and it involves no vision–language pairs, seeds, cross-model maps or shared features. That is a related but different construct from every version: within-model cross-modal alignment and its functional consequences. It does not cite or test the Platonic Representation Hypothesis or convergent learning. Its findings are recorded under fits_no_version, not as tests. The record's T5 and V6/V7 links are therefore withdrawn.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors add that late attention allocation causally affects answer-code separation (not correctness) in Qwen2.5-Omni, and that compression repairs a subset of speech-only errors.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses cross-layer linear CKA with DTW-aligned speech and text states, then compares layer-wise answer margins; it does not conduct the original claim’s model-scale/performance convergence test.
record.method_sensitivity: DTW best-match path diagnostics are more sensitive at base layer 0 than at higher bases; width-64 band leaves the reported path statistics unchanged. Middle-layer CKA lift and band persist without interpolation or averaging against position-permutation baselines. Alignment-free matched-versus-deranged results are mixed across the four model–benchmark cells.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen2.5-Omni and MiniCPM-o, speech and text routes form a broad middle-layer CKA band. The band exceeds position-permutation baselines (ΔA .09–.13, positive 95% CIs). Alignment-free cross-item CKA is mixed: 1 of 4 cells meets all criteria.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Speech and text inputs to a speech LLM converge to similar middle-layer representations within the shared backbone.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen2-Audio shows weak speech–text CKA through the middle layers (row maxima ≤0.07/0.13), rising only at the final layers. LLaMA-Omni shows broad, non-layer-specific similarity. Within-model cross-modal alignment thus differs by model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The degree of within-model cross-modal alignment varies across speech LLMs; weaker speech performance co-occurs with weaker alignment in one model.

fits_no_version.finding: Despite middle-layer alignment, late-layer answer margins differ between speech and text routes. The crossover contrast is +0.3652 [0.287, 0.443] for Qwen2.5-Omni on BBH.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric (CKA) alignment between representations does not imply functional equivalence in how they are used.

fits_no_version.finding: The best-match path from DTW-aligned CKA is sensitive to DTW base layer 0 (R² ≤0.75 vs ≥0.80 at higher bases). The width-64 band changes nothing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-modal layer-correspondence diagnostics depend on alignment-method settings.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 (40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems, as stated in the paper)
record.problems: The evidence concerns four accessible speech LLMs around the 7B scale and semantics-matched speech/text tasks, not scale or capability trends across diverse architectures, objectives, and training data. The native-length CKA robustness sample uses 100 items per benchmark. Alignment-free results are mixed. Some answer-margin comparisons are conditioned on observed free-generation outcomes; the paper notes answer-formatting issues for some models and does not identify the upstream cause of the modality gap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant convergence results omitted. Behavioral accuracy gaps, compression repairs, and attention-edit effects are not direct tests of representation convergence; the paper itself distinguishes answer-code separation from correctness.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models or any scale trend.
No vision–language models. The speech–text comparison is within one model, not between separately trained encoders. No relation of alignment to capability is tested.
The DTW and pooling sensitivity checks concern within-model speech–text alignment, not cross-model convergence.
No cross-model alignment levels or causes are tested.

record.verdict_notes: Withdrew all version links. The comparison is between input modalities of a single jointly trained model, not between independently trained models or separate vision and language models. The closest analogue is V2, but the system kind and the capability-scaling relation both differ. The paper does not cite PRH or convergent learning.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep or comparison relating model size or capability to alignment; no test across independently trained architectures, objectives, and data.

No vision–language models, and no test of alignment increasing as both models improve. The study measures speech–text alignment, but this is not the vision–language and performance-scaling relationship specified by this version.
No comparison of different initialization seeds for the same architecture or shared features/subspaces across seeds.
No test of mapping one model’s representations to another’s, layer stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

No out-of-distribution evaluation or broad comparison of alternative representation-similarity measures. Setting checks include DTW base layer, DTW cost/band, pooling, position permutations, and benchmarks.

The study documents incomplete or differing speech–text alignment and divergence in answer margins, but does not test whether alignment plateaus as scale grows or whether shared training data/objectives cause it.

rows.operation_detail: Native-length cross-modal linear CKA; middle-layer lift and band width compared with a position-permutation baseline.

conditions.value: one native speech state per text token; no interpolation or within-group averaging

rows.measure: Middle-layer CKA lift ΔA and band width ΔW.95 above position-permutation baseline

rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap intervals as shown for both values
rows.note: The paper reports positive lift and a broad band under this native-length measurement.
rows.check: Within-model speech–text CKA lift; not cross-model convergence, so no version applies.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-Omni
rows.operation_detail: Swept DTW base layer, distance cost, and width-64 band; reported sensitivity of the cross-layer best-match path.
rows.measure: Best-match path linearity R² and stall fraction
rows.baseline: Higher DTW base layers: path linearity R² ≥ 0.80 in all four panels
rows.value: At base layer 0, path linearity R² ≤ 0.75; stall fraction highest at base layer 0 in three of four panels. Width-64 band leaves both statistics unchanged in every setting.
rows.note: These are best-match path diagnostics, not reported CKA values. The paper says base layer 0 is more sensitive than higher bases.
rows.check: DTW sensitivity of the best-match path, a diagnostic of the study's own alignment method. It is not a similarity-measure dependence of cross-model convergence.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: DTW base-layer settings in the Qwen2.5-Omni path diagnostic
reader_labels.reason: Base layer 0 has lower path linearity and a higher stall fraction in most panels, although the width-64 band changes neither statistic; this is path sensitivity rather than a demonstrated disappearance of CKA alignment (R13).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Middle-layer CKA maxima remain low and the expected band is absent, while speech answer readouts are weak or negative in the reported conditions (R9, R10, R27, R28).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Qwen2.5-Omni and MiniCPM-o on semantics-matched benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: These models show a middle-layer speech–text CKA band, but Qwen2.5-Omni’s late margins cross over by which route answers correctly, and MiniCPM-o’s late speech margins differ from text margins (R5, R6, R7, R8, R18, R19, R20, R21, R22, R23, R24).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Similarity is broad and less layer-specific, while late margins in the text-only-correct groups favor text and diverge in sign (R11, R12, R25, R26).
